skill.description: Guide for benchmarking FlashInfer kernels with CUPTI timing and CUDA event fallback.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and fenced examples in SKILL.md. One high-severity issue is confirmed because the troubleshooting section recommends a sudo nvidia-smi command that changes GPU clock settings. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or network reconnaissance intent was found.

remediation.issue: Privileged GPU clock command in troubleshooting guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the sudo command, or mark it as manual-only with user confirmation, impact notes, and a rollback command.

remediation.issue: Command examples are presented without an explicit execution boundary.
remediation.suggestion: State that benchmark commands are examples and must not run without user review and environment confirmation.

content.value_statement: GPU kernel benchmarks can be noisy when timing includes host overhead or missing warmups. This skill guides FlashInfer users through CUPTI timing, backend comparison, and reproducible CSV results.
actual_capabilities: Explains CUPTI timing and CUDA event fallback for FlashInfer benchmarks.
Shows how to run single FlashInfer benchmark routines with backend comparisons.
Guides batch benchmark setup with test lists and CSV output.
Demonstrates custom kernel timing with bench_gpu_time in Python.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for CUPTI, variance, reference checks, and backend support.
limitations: Requires an existing FlashInfer checkout with benchmark scripts available.
Accurate CUPTI timing depends on compatible CUDA and cupti-python versions.
Benchmark results depend on GPU model, drivers, clocks, and backend support.
It provides guidance, not an automated benchmark runner.

use_cases.title: Compare Kernel Backends
use_cases.description: Compare FlashInfer routines across FA2, FA3, cuDNN, CUTLASS, and TensorRT-LLM backends with consistent parameters.

use_cases.title: Create Reproducible Performance Reports
use_cases.description: Run repeatable measurements, capture median time and throughput, and save results for later analysis.

use_cases.title: Validate Deployment Hardware
use_cases.description: Check which backend performs best on target GPUs before changing model serving configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Single Benchmark
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one FlashInfer routine.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a FlashInfer benchmark for [routine] on [GPU]. Use these shapes: [shape details]. Include warmup, iterations, and reference checks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Backends
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate backend comparison for one workload.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a FlashInfer backend comparison for [routine]. Compare [backends], explain key flags, and tell me which metrics to review.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Batch Benchmark
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a batch FlashInfer benchmark list for [routines] across [batch sizes] and [sequence lengths]. Include CSV output and reproducibility guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Timing Variance
prompt_templates.prompt: My FlashInfer benchmark results have high standard deviation. Diagnose likely causes and propose a controlled retest plan using CUPTI or CUDA events.

output_examples.input: I need to benchmark decode attention on an H100 and compare FA2, FA2 tensor cores, and cuDNN.
output_examples.output: A benchmark plan with required shape parameters, backend selection, warmup settings, reference checking, and CSV result capture.

output_examples.input: CUPTI is not installed, but I still need useful FlashInfer timing results.
output_examples.output: A fallback plan that uses CUDA events, explains expected accuracy limits, and identifies when CUPTI is worth installing.

output_examples.input: Several backends produce different outputs during reference checks.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist for precision differences, tolerance review, verbose statistics, and safe handling of output mismatches.

best_practices: Enable reference checks when comparing backend correctness.
Use warmup iterations and enough measurement iterations before interpreting results.
Save CSV outputs with clear case tags for later comparison.
anti_patterns: Comparing backends with different shapes, dtypes, or sequence lengths.
Treating CUDA event timing as identical to CUPTI timing for very short kernels.
Running privileged GPU clock commands without approval and a rollback plan.

faq.question: Does this skill run benchmarks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and command patterns for running FlashInfer benchmarks in your own environment.

faq.question: Is CUPTI required?
faq.answer: No. CUPTI is preferred for accuracy, but FlashInfer can fall back to CUDA event timing.

faq.question: Which FlashInfer routines are covered?
faq.answer: The guide covers attention, FP8 and FP4 GEMM, and mixture-of-experts benchmark routines listed in the skill.

faq.question: Can it compare multiple backends?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to compare backends such as FA2, FA3, cuDNN, CUTLASS, and TensorRT-LLM.

faq.question: What outputs should I expect?
faq.answer: Typical outputs include median kernel time, standard deviation, throughput metrics, and optional CSV records.

faq.question: What should I check before trusting results?
faq.answer: Check reference correctness, warmup count, iteration count, GPU stability, and whether CUPTI or CUDA events were used.
